activity_b.text: Hi Anura, you look tired and a bit stressed today.
What’s going on?
Are you working on something urgent, or is it just one of those long days?
Hi Nimal.
Yes, it’s been a hectic morning.
I’m preparing a short presentation for Monday, and I’m trying to get everything ready before the end of the day.
I’m updating a few figures and answering emails at the same time.
To make matters worse, my computer is running very slowly today.
Oh dear!
When technology acts up, everything feels harder.
Are you staying late at the office this evening to finish everything, or are you leaving on time?
No, I’m not staying late.
I have to leave by six.
I’m travelling to Kandy this evening and I’m meeting my sister at the bus stand.
We often go home together for the weekend.
Today, too, we’re catching the same bus and heading straight home.
That sounds nice.
Are you spending the whole weekend there, or are you coming back to Colombo early?
I’m staying until Sunday afternoon.
Tomorrow morning, we’re cleaning the house and preparing food for a small family gathering.
It’s my parents’ thirtieth wedding anniversary.
Approximately twenty people are coming for lunch, so the house will be quite busy.
I can imagine.
Family events are always fun.
So, what are your plans for Sunday then?
Are you meeting friends, or are you just taking it easy with your family?
On Sunday morning, I’m visiting my uncle, and I’m helping him with some paperwork.
He doesn’t know how to use a computer, so I usually sort these things out for him.
After that, I’m returning to Colombo.
A friend is giving me a ride, so I hope to be back in Colombo by seven.
And then?
Do you have anything planned for the evening?
In the evening, I might watch a movie with friends or go out to Galle Face—I’m not sure yet.
But I’m not staying out late because I’m starting work at six a.m. on Monday.
Alright then.
Have a good weekend, and I’ll see you on Monday.
Thanks, Nimal.
You too.
See you on Monday.
